thread:
alex: heads-up — i'm taking the night handoff. primary = alex, secondary = sara. i'm OOO from 03:00-06:00 UTC so jordan will cover that window.

alex: quick note on coverage gaps: we have no on-site infra person between 02:00-04:00 PST. if a hardware ticket shows up ping @infra-oncall, otherwise escalate to @eng-sre.

oncall-bot: <incident created> severity: P2 — increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate in eu-west-1. pager: @alex @sara. (incident id: INC-20251005-73)

alex: saw the bot — short checklist below for whoever answers first. copy-paste into the incident timeline.

alex: QUICK REMEDY CHEAT: 
1) Check model-serving pool health: `curl -s http://metrics.internal/serving/pool?region=eu-west-1`
2) If pool saturation > 80%: scale group by +1 (autoscale-cmd) or failover to dedicated pool.
3) If errors look like OOMs, switch to fallback model variant `redwood-7b-quant` for the route.
4) Check prefix cache hit rate — if cache miss spike, check cache node health and restart `cache-proxy` on node with highest misses.
5) If latency spike + 5xx: flip traffic to eu-west-2 or region fallback policy.

alex: links: 
- runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/incidents/api-5xx-mitigation
- handoff playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/oncall/night-handoff
- quick ops commands: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/ops/quick-commands

sara: adding small triage steps — check the model runtime logs for `KV cache miss` and `alloc failed`. those two patterns usually mean quantization mismatch or bad cache eviction.

jordan: noted. if this is a release-related regression, check deploy-bot for recent deploys.

deploy-bot: deploys in last 2 hours: 
- service/serving-edge @ 2025-10-05T00:40Z (hash: d4c3b2) -> route /v1/generate
- infra/cache-proxy @ 2025-10-04T22:10Z (hash: a1b2c3)

lee: i'm on-call infra backup for the night. if it looks like bad cache nodes restart them in this order: cache-02 -> cache-05 -> cache-03. 

lee: restart command: 
```
sudo systemctl restart redwood-cache-proxy
journalctl -u redwood-cache-proxy -n 200 | tail -n 50
```

alex: escalation thresholds reminder: 
- Page primary for p1/p2. p3 can go to #eng-oncall async.
- If customer SLA impacted (>= 3 customers with errors in last 10m) escalate to @support-lead and start incident bridge.

jordan: i'm seeing a small spike in EV cache misses from 23:58 -> 00:02 UTC. logs show `alloc failed` on model shard 4. i'm going to switch route to `redwood-7b-quant` for canary 10%

sara: +1 on rollback if deploy points to serving-edge hash d4c3b2. if rollback needed follow runbook step 4 (hot rollback) and notify customers via support playbook.

alex: reminder: document everything in the incident timeline. use this template: 
- symptom: short sentence
- initial triage steps taken
- mitigation applied (with timestamps)
- next steps and owners

alex: quick checklist summary to paste into timeline and chat: 
- who answered page: <@alex>
- primary/secondary: alex/sara
- coverage gap: 02:00-04:00 PST (jordan covers 03:00-06:00 UTC)
- runbook links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/incidents/api-5xx-mitigation 
- immediate mitigations attempted: scale +1, route 10% to fallback model, restart cache-proxy on cache-02

jordan: done route switch to fallback (10%) at 2025-10-05T00:05Z. watching for error rate to drop.

oncall-bot: metric alert cleared: 5xx rate back to baseline in eu-west-1 at 2025-10-05T00:12Z. incident auto-resolve scheduled in 10m unless reopened.

alex: thanks team. leave any postmortem notes in the incident doc. i'll write a short blameless RCA if it stays resolved.

lee: adding a note — let's add a short doc to the handoff page with the explicit cache node restart order and common grep patterns that saved time tonight.

sara: agree. i'll create a tiny PR to handoff playbook with those grep snippets after the incident doc is stable. :thumbsup:

alex: closing thread for handoff — if anything reappears ping @pagerduty and start the bridge.

alex: TL;DR: primary/secondary assigned, coverage gap called out, runbook links + quick commands provided, immediate mitigations applied (scale, fallback model, restart cache).
